data.title: Open IP Camera Firmware
data.author: zakki
data.article_summary: OpenIPC是一个开源的IP摄像头固件，旨在替代厂商预装的封闭、不安全且常被弃更的固件。它支持ARM和MIPS处理器，提供预编译二进制文件和完整源代码，采用MIT许可证，允许代码重用于任何目的，包括专有软件。OpenIPC提供自由和安全性，用户可完全控制摄像头，避免后门和恶意软件。它支持多种摄像头，基础功能包括视频和音频流。此外，还支持外部云存储、YouTube和Telegram流媒体、SOCKS5代理、虚拟隧道等功能。另有针对无人机、安全头盔、医疗研究等特殊设备的版本。使用OpenIPC于军事目的不被允许，商业使用需联系项目方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IP摄像头选择及相关开源支持

不同观点：
• **cnst的观点**：Wansview Q5和Cinnado D1是较为便宜且受thingino支持的摄像头选择。他提供了具体的亚马逊链接和价格，指出这些型号可以在FBA（Fulfillment by Amazon）下以较低价格购买。此外，他提到开源安全摄像头支持在美国并不普遍，反而在东欧和中国更为先进。

• **miiiiiike的观点**：对选择IP摄像头感到困惑，特别是品牌和可靠性方面。他特别关注支持PoE（Power over Ethernet）的室内外摄像头，且对成本不敏感，更注重可靠性和开源支持。

• **roacato的观点**：提到OpenIPC项目的主录制/编码应用程序（majestic）并非完全开源，而thingino项目则提供了完全开源的解决方案，许多开发者已经转向thingino。

• **pbasista的观点**：认为目前的开源固件不支持主流品牌如Hikvision，并指出高端摄像头在性能上的优势（如8MP传感器支持4K@25 fps）。他希望能有支持高端摄像头的开源固件。

• **infogulch的观点**：关注thingino是否能与开源NVR（网络视频录像机）软件如Shinobi、Frigate和ZoneMinder兼容，并提供了相关链接。

• **roscas的观点**：分享了使用tp-link "tapo"家用摄像头的负面体验，指出其需要永久互联网连接，并对这种设计表示不满。

• **happyPersonR的观点**：询问是否有已知的兼容摄像头型号列表，并对该项目表示兴趣。

• **boredemployee的观点**：寻找开源且可靠的AI算法实现，用于人脸识别、人数统计等功能，并提到有人建议“不惜一切代价避免使用yolo”，寻求其他替代方案。

• **systemswizard的观点**：简短地表示对这个项目的赞赏。

• **ck2的观点**：提到thingino可以控制一些他的摄像头，并提供了一个英文翻译链接，指出该项目的一些功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于开源固件对高端摄像头的支持不足，以及用户对摄像头可靠性和开源解决方案的需求。
• 用户对AI算法在摄像头中的应用表现出兴趣，尤其是开源和自建硬件的结合。
• 对不同品牌和型号的摄像头进行了价格和功能上的比较，特别是低价摄像头与高端摄像头的对比。

44758463.article_content:
OpenIPC is an alternative open firmware for your IP camera.
OpenIPC is an open source operating system from the open community targeting for IP cameras with ARM and MIPS processors from several manufacturers in order to replace that closed, opaque, insecure, often abandoned and unsupported firmware pre-installed by a vendor.
OpenIPC Firmware comes as binary pre-compiled files for easy installation by end-user. Also, we provide full access to the source files for further development and improvement by any capable programmer willing to contribute to the project. OpenIPC source code is released under one of the most simple open source license agreements,
MIT License
, giving users express permission to reuse code for any purpose, even as part of a proprietary software. We only ask you politely to contribute your improvements back to us and also be sure to contact us if you use our project for
commercial purposes
. We would be grateful for any feedback and suggestions. The use of the OpenIPC project and its components for military purposes is not permitted.
Installation Instructions
Precompiled binary files
Source code on GitHub
OpenIPC Firmware uses
Buildroot
to build its Linux distro, and utilizes either
Majestic
,
Divinus
,
Mini
or
Venc
streamer.
Majestic code while is not open, provides unprecedented performance and capabilities for a wide range of hardware. The author of Majestic streamer is looking into possibilities to open-source the codebase after he secures enough funds to support further open development. You can
help
to make it happen sooner.
Why OpenIPC Firmware?
First of all, OpenIPC Firmware brings you freedom. With OpenIPC on your camera you are the master of your streams. You have full access to the system and can control what, where, and how you want your camera to behave. There are no backdoors, no botnets, no crypto-mining malware, no keyloggers, no password sniffers, nothing you could possibly expect in a closed binary system with no access to its source code.
As for the Firmware capabilities, we strive to provide universal support for a wide range of cameras, thus we are focused on basic functionality first, allowing end-users to upgrade their cameras' firmware and stream video and audio (where supported) without too much hassle.
We have some interesting bits though. Our Firmware supports external IPEYE cloud storage, streaming video to Youtube and Telegram, using SOCKS5 proxy, setting up a Virtual Tunnel, and more.
There are also several projects focused on specialized equipment, such as a camera to be mounted on a drone, for mounting on construction helmets, for use in surveying tools, for medical research of the organs of vision, underwater fishing, etc.

data.title: How we built Bluey’s world
data.author: skrebbel
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了《Bluey》动画的原创艺术总监Catriona Drummond如何打造该剧的场景和背景。Catriona详细描述了从收集布里斯班的视觉参考资料，到通过风格化建筑、色彩和光线，创建出独特的Heelers家庭世界，以及制定展示视觉风格的“风格圣经”的过程。她将自己在布里斯班的生活经验融入到剧中，捕捉该城市的美好与特色，使《Bluey》的场景既亲切又充满魅力。Catriona在23岁时成为澳大利亚最年轻的动画节目首席艺术总监，她与创作者Joe Brumm密切合作，实现了展示布里斯班之美的共同愿景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕动画片《Bluey》的讨论，包括其情感影响、艺术表现、与其他儿童节目的比较以及其成功背后的原因。

不同观点：
• **乡愁与地域代表性**：
  - [rmccue] 指出《Bluey》唤起了他们对昆士兰的乡愁，认为该节目真实地展现了昆士兰州的风貌，而不是像其他澳大利亚媒体那样将场景设定为悉尼、墨尔本或内陆地区。他们提到，在成长过程中很少能看到与自己生活相关的本地媒体。
  - [valtism] 作为布里斯班居民，证实了该节目很好地捕捉了这座城市的色彩，特别是其独特的金色黄昏。

• **艺术与故事叙述**：
  - [x187463] 赞扬《Bluey》的艺术风格，认为其色彩丰富且线条清晰，故事叙述注重角色和情感，而非追求最大化观众注意力。他们还提到节目节奏合适，适合限制屏幕时间。
  - [asciii] 强调《Bluey》的艺术吸引力，认为即使静音观看也具有吸引力，音乐进一步提升了观赏体验。

• **与其他儿童节目的比较**：
  - [hollywood_court] 认为《Bluey》是他们看过的最好的儿童节目，相比之下《Peppa Pig》显得逊色，他们的孩子也不再想看《Peppa Pig》。
  - [nmfisher] 则偏好《Peppa Pig》，因为其色彩方案能让孩子在15-20分钟后更容易自然脱离屏幕。

• **节目制作与幕后故事**：
  - [tomhow] 提到《Bluey》的沉浸式景点“Bluey’s World”，并推荐如果有机会去布里斯班，非常值得一看。
  - [donpott] 提到之前关于《Bluey》的文章曾引起广泛讨论，提供了相关链接供参考。
  - [Amorymeltzer] 推荐了播客“20 Thousand Hertz”，其中详细探讨了《Bluey》的声音设计和配音，显示了制作团队在各个方面的用心。

补充讨论：
• **个人体验与推荐**：
  - [aaronbrethorst] 提到《Bluey》中的某些情节和场景让他们感到愉悦，甚至比他们的孩子更喜欢这个节目。
  - [twalkz] 推荐成年人如果不知道看什么，可以尝试《Bluey》的某一集，特别是第二季第26集“Sleepy time”。

• **节目长度与观看体验**：
  - [x187463] 提到每集约7分钟的长度非常适合家庭限制屏幕时间，提供了一个自然的停止点。

争议的焦点：
• **节目对孩子的吸引力与脱离难度**：
  - [nmfisher] 认为《Bluey》的色彩设计对孩子吸引力过强，导致孩子难以自然脱离，而《Peppa Pig》则更易于让孩子在适当时间停止观看。
  - 其他评论则多集中于赞扬《Bluey》的艺术和情感深度，并未提及类似问题。

整体来看，评论主要围绕《Bluey》在情感、艺术和地域代表性方面的成功，同时也有一些关于其与其他儿童节目对比的讨论。

How we built Bluey’s world: tales from original series art director, Catriona Drummond
Catriona walks us through the creation of the beloved cartoon’s scenery and backgrounds, from its dollhouse proportions and subtle doggy details, to its distinctly Brisbanite atmosphere.

Bluey
is one of the best kids TV shows ever made – fact. Part of its overall brilliance is its utterly charming and beautiful scenery, which was designed and established by lead art director on series one (and some of series two), Catriona Drummond. Set in Brisbane, Australia, where Catriona is from, the artist brought not only her creative talents but her intrinsic understanding of the city’s landscape to the show. Here, we republish an excerpt of her Substack series
Creating Bluey: Tales from the Art Director
, in particular the article laying bare her process of designing the show’s backgrounds – from gathering visual reference material of Brisbane, to stylising its architecture, colour and light, while building the shape language and proportions for the Heelers’ world, and creating a “style bible” for the show’s visual universe. Read the rest of the series on Catriona’s Substack, Goodsniff,
here
.

When I was approached by Joe Brumm, the creator of
Bluey
, to be its lead art director in 2017, it wasn’t out of the (excuse the pun) blue. I had graduated in 2014, so was relatively fresh out of university, mostly freelancing in advertising doing 2D animation. Every job I took, I tried to inch closer to what I really wanted to do: work in visual development for animated film and television. Living in Australia, there weren’t a lot of prospects for such things. It always felt a little like I was born at the wrong place at the wrong time to do what I really dreamed of.
I had met Joe at the Melbourne International Animation Festival and had made sure to always keep in contact with him to let him know when I was available for work. As, at the time, Joe wasn’t ‘The Creator of
Bluey’,
but the owner of his own animation company, Studio Joho – one of the few studios in Brisbane doing 2D animation work.
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
We finally ended up back in each other’s orbits in 2017 working on a few different projects at Ludo Studio, a Brisbane production company that had started producing some 2D shows. All the while bubbling away in the background was this little show called
Bluey
that Ludo and Joe were trying to get funding for. Somewhere amongst all this, Joe sent me the pilot he’d made, asking whether I’d be interested in hopping on board as art director. Against all odds, I would be getting to do what I’d always dreamed of. And at 23, as far as I know, I was about to become Australia’s youngest lead art director for an animated show.
Joe kicked off the project with a singular and solidified vision for the show’s art direction. He wanted Bluey’s visuals to be beautiful, and show off our hometown of Brisbane, which we both cared so much about. To be honest it was an easy brief, because every other day in Brisbane the weather was so unbelievably good, the everyday scenery so breathtaking, you never wanted to leave. For locals, it was the little secret we kept to ourselves: that Brisbane was the best city in the world. But in starting work on Bluey, we were really about to blow the lid on that.
The initial design phases of Bluey involved tapping into this beauty, as well as employing many fundamental animation design principles. Here, I’ve put together a step-by-step process of how it was done.
Above

Above

Step 1: Reference Gathering
For every visual development project, the first thing I do before I even put pen to paper is gather reference. Both photographs and artistic inspiration. data.title: KDE Plasma prepares crackdown on focus-stealing window behavior under Wayland
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Wayland通过"XDG Activation"机制有效防止窗口焦点被窃取，解决X11中焦点窃取带来的困扰和安全风险。在Wayland下，应用程序需向合成器请求一次性激活令牌以获取焦点，防止未授权窗口擅自获取焦点。KDE开发者Kai-Uwe Broulik计划在KWin中严格执行此机制，新增"极端"焦点防窃设置，确保窗口仅在拥有有效令牌时才能激活。此举解决了多个问题，如Dolphin文件管理器和KRunner等工具的正确激活。同时，后端改进如DBusRunner的SetActivationToken方法确保了文件打开时焦点的正确处理。这一系列改进来源于KDE对Wayland更严格焦点管理的探索。

44784312.article_content:
One of the most
interesting things about Wayland
is how it handles window focus, unlike X11, where focus stealing can be frustrating and even a security risk. Its main advantage is a mechanism that prevents focus stealing. The protocol that plays a role in this is known as "XDG Activation."
Here's how it works: Say you double-click a PDF file in your file manager. The file manager first asks the Wayland compositor for a special, single-use "activation token". This request is tied directly to your click, proving a human wanted this to happen.
The file manager then launches your PDF viewer and hands it the token. The PDF viewer, upon starting, shows this token to the compositor and asks to be activated. The compositor checks if the token is legit and, if so, gives the PDF viewer focus.
If the token is missing, old, or otherwise invalid, the compositor says no. The viewer window will not get focus, and instead, its icon in the taskbar will start flashing to grab your attention.
Flashing icon in the taskbar | Image:
Kai-Uwe Broulik
Kai-Uwe Broulik, a KDE developer, recently wrote about the plan to "switch on KWin’s focus stealing on Wayland at a low level". This means KWin, the window manager for KDE Plasma, will begin enforcing this properly.
Under X11, new or dialog windows can only grab focus if their application was most recently active, a check often based on a timestamp called
_NET_WM_USER_TIME
. It was a flimsy system at best. For example, Kai cited how the prevention logic on X11 would sometimes stop the Adobe Flash Player fullscreen window from showing on top of a YouTube video. On X11, an application could just call
XSetInputFocus
on another app's window, and while KWin would try to undo it, focus did flicker for a moment.
Over on Wayland, things are much better with XDG Activation, but some apps still violate the protocol through improper usage. In situations like that, KWin would, by default, just focus any new window that opened. This is changing.
A new "Extreme" setting for "Focus Stealing Prevention" in the Window Management settings will force KWin to activate a window if and only if it requests activation with a valid token.
Image:
Kai-Uwe Broulik
Using this stricter mode, developers Xaver Hugl and Kai-Uwe Broulik have already fixed a ton of issues, introducing several key changes:
Dolphin no longer discards its activation token when launching a new instance.
KRunner, Kickoff, and other Plasmoid popups now correctly request activation.
LayerShell-Qt now requests activation on show and properly reads the
XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN
from the environment.
Allowing privileged clients like Plasma to request tokens correctly.
Ignoring modifier key presses for focus prevention logic, since they are often part of a global shortcut.
The work extends to the backend as well, with the DBusRunner specification now gaining a
SetActivationToken
method that is called just before an action runs. Baloo, the desktop search runner, now uses this to ensure that opening files in an existing application window works correctly.
You can learn more on
Kai's blog post.

data.title: Read your code
data.author: noeclement
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在2025年使用AI编程工具开发项目时，开发者应注意的问题，尤其是要**阅读代码**。文章提出了"氛围编码"（vibe-coding）的概念，即人类与AI进行对话式编码，人类指导，AI实现。然而，这种方法有三大风险：

1. **架构弱化**：不审查AI生成的代码会导致架构逐渐崩溃，不良设计可能成为常态。
2. **实现知识丧失**：仅关注结果会导致开发者丧失对代码实现细节的理解，影响创意和技术决策。
3. **安全漏洞**：忽视代码审查可能引发安全问题，许多安全问题依赖知识和经验避免。

文章建议，开发者应像对待新手开发者一样对待AI，审查其生成的代码，并保持对代码质量和安全的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Vibe-Coding”（氛围编码）以及使用AI生成代码的实践和争议

不同观点：
• **Simonw**：支持Vibe-Coding的定义，认为这是一种人类指导、AI实现的对话式编码过程，并将这种实践与Steve Yegge的“CHOP”（面向聊天的编程）相比较。Simonw更认同Karpathy的定义，认为一旦开始审查代码，就不再是纯粹的Vibe-Coding。
• **Ericpauley**：认为AI在处理低价值、重复性任务（如样板代码、CRUD操作）时表现良好，但在处理复杂、创新功能时表现较差。AI工具能提升有经验开发者的生产力，但会降低仅处理简单任务的开发者的价值。
• **MomsAVoxell**：强烈反对Vibe-Coding，认为AI/ML应被视为初级程序员，其代码必须经过审查和理解。强调遵循软件开发流程和最佳实践的重要性，反对“敏捷黑客”式的开发方式。
• **Andix**：认为与AI合作类似于与团队中的初级开发者合作，需要高级开发者提供方向和组织代码。缺乏高级职位的项目经验会使与AI合作变得困难。
• **Alphazard**：不愿阅读AI生成的代码，认为AI的存在是为了减少处理复杂任务的需要。仅在AI生成代码无效时才介入，并从顶层开始实现。
• **Joe8756438**：认为当前理解代码的唯一方法是阅读它，不阅读代码存在风险。尽管AI可以生成代码，但阅读代码仍是最佳实践。
• **Vermon**：认为Vibe-Coding的定义就是不看代码，一旦阅读代码就不再是“氛围编码”。
• **Yanis_t**：认为依赖AI生成代码能提高生产力，最终需要放手让AI自主完成任务。
• **Kbrannigan**：将AI生成代码与早期手写汇编代码对比，认为使用AI生成代码是编程进化的自然过程。
• **_jab**：认为Vibe-Coding的效果取决于对代码样貌的清晰想象，越清晰越能快速判断AI输出是否合理。
• **Ollysb**：认为可以不阅读代码成为架构师，通过详细的前期规划和架构审查来确保代码质量。
• **Fxtentacle**：认为不阅读AI生成代码的建议是不切实际的，如同建议盲人仔细看路。
• **Chanux**：引用了Peter Naur的“编程即理论构建”文章，提供相关阅读材料以深入理解讨论。
• **Jedimastert**：对评论区中许多人愿意不经过审查就将AI生成的代码纳入代码库表示惊讶和质疑。
• **Chrisjj**：认为不审查AI生成代码会导致严重问题，并指出这种要求可能会导致不称职的程序员失去工作。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：核心争议在于是否应审查AI生成的代码。一方认为审查是确保代码质量和降低风险的必要步骤，另一方认为不阅读代码、依赖AI生成是提高生产力的途径。
• **AI的角色定位**：讨论中对AI在开发中的角色有不同看法，有人将其视为初级程序员，有人认为其仅在处理简单任务时有效，还有人认为其能大幅提升高级开发者的生产力。
• **开发流程和最佳实践**：强调遵循软件开发流程和最佳实践的重要性，反对“敏捷黑客”式的开发方式，强调代码审查、测试和验证。

总结：讨论围绕Vibe-Coding的定义、AI生成代码的审查必要性、AI在开发中的角色以及开发流程和最佳实践展开，展示了多种观点和实践经验的碰撞。

44785562.article_content:
Read That F*cking Code!
8 Mar, 2025
|
Edit page
If you’d told me 2–3 years ago that in 2025, one of my top pieces of advice for the new generation of developers would be “
read your code
” (we’re not even talking about re-reading it)… I’m not sure I would’ve believed you.
What This Article Covers
I’m not here to lecture anyone, but
if you’re aiming to build serious projects
these days, it might be worth learning how to approach AI coding tools the right way.
This post covers:
Three critical risks of poor
vibe-coding
practices
Two effective approaches for production-grade AI-assisted development
Practical tips to maintain code quality while leveraging AI speed
Vibe-Coding Refresh
Maybe it’s time we take a fresh look at what vibe-coding actually is. It’s more than just hobby prompting to get code — it’s a practice that serious developers should learn to master. What it means to me:
Vibe-Coding is a dialogue-based coding process between a human and an AI where the human guides and the AI implements.
It’s possible to ship code without ever reading it.
Since Claude Code and Windsurf arrived, it’s now totally possible to get working results without reading a single line of code. You can vibe-code without ever leaving your chat window and just operate based on outcomes - I’ve tried that, out of curiosity.
Even if it doesn’t work on the first try (though it often does), you just explain what’s wrong, and voilà — working result incoming.
But This Comes With Three Critical Issues
1. A Weakened Architecture
Not reviewing AI-generated code
will
lead to serious problems.
First up: the slow but sure breakdown of your architecture… assuming you even took the time to plan one in the first place.
From experience, even with well-crafted prompts and clearly defined plans for a new feature, Claude Code (which I love, by the way) still sometimes goes off-script. Make sure to properly configure your @CLAUDE.md files to avoid this as much as possible.
Example of architectural drift:

);
}
}

// Business logic creeping into controllers

/profile/:id
'
,

(

=>

const

=

(

.

// Formatting logic that belongs in service layer
const

=

+

If you don’t catch it early, those small inconsistencies become part of the codebase—and your favorite assistant will be tempted to follow those bad examples in the future.
You’re still the architect!
Everyone keeps saying it these days: treat your AI like a (brilliant) new junior dev
1
. And what does a junior dev do before starting a new feature? They read through the existing codebase. Which means any weak or messy design choices are likely to get repeated.
And by the way, you’d never push junior dev code without reviewing it.
Now more than ever, we’re all responsible for the architecture. We spend more time guiding the AI on how to code than writing the actual code ourselves.
2. Loss of Implementation Knowledge
You cannot delegate the act of thinking.
Alain (French philosopher, 19th century)

you won’t own your domain anymore
.
Why does that matter?
In every experience I’ve had — especially when building my latest startup

— I’ve learned that apps and features don’t take shape at implementation time. They’re designed upstream: business rules, tech and infrastructure decisions all take form before you touch the keyboard. They come to you while commuting, while chatting, or—often—while in the shower.
Depending on your level of responsibility, you may or may not be involved outside of work. But you’ll probably agree that your best ‘Aha!’ moments didn’t happen in front of VS Code.
If you don’t have the structure of your domain — its concepts and abstractions — constantly simmering somewhere in the back of your mind, you won’t be able to fully leverage the creative potential of modern tech.

44785562.article_summary:
本文讨论了在2025年使用AI编程工具开发项目时，开发者应注意的问题，尤其是要**阅读代码**。文章提出了"氛围编码"（vibe-coding）的概念，即人类与AI进行对话式编码，人类指导，AI实现。然而，这种方法有三大风险：

1. **架构弱化**：不审查AI生成的代码会导致架构逐渐崩溃，不良设计可能成为常态。
2. **实现知识丧失**：仅关注结果会导致开发者丧失对代码实现细节的理解，影响创意和技术决策。
3. **安全漏洞**：忽视代码审查可能引发安全问题，许多安全问题依赖知识和经验避免。

文章建议，开发者应像对待新手开发者一样对待AI，审查其生成的代码，并保持对代码质量和安全的关注。
44785562.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Vibe-Coding”（氛围编码）以及使用AI生成代码的实践和争议

不同观点：
• **Simonw**：支持Vibe-Coding的定义，认为这是一种人类指导、AI实现的对话式编码过程，并将这种实践与Steve Yegge的“CHOP”（面向聊天的编程）相比较。Simonw更认同Karpathy的定义，认为一旦开始审查代码，就不再是纯粹的Vibe-Coding。
• **Ericpauley**：认为AI在处理低价值、重复性任务（如样板代码、CRUD操作）时表现良好，但在处理复杂、创新功能时表现较差。AI工具能提升有经验开发者的生产力，但会降低仅处理简单任务的开发者的价值。
• **MomsAVoxell**：强烈反对Vibe-Coding，认为AI/ML应被视为初级程序员，其代码必须经过审查和理解。强调遵循软件开发流程和最佳实践的重要性，反对“敏捷黑客”式的开发方式。
• **Andix**：认为与AI合作类似于与团队中的初级开发者合作，需要高级开发者提供方向和组织代码。缺乏高级职位的项目经验会使与AI合作变得困难。
• **Alphazard**：不愿阅读AI生成的代码，认为AI的存在是为了减少处理复杂任务的需要。仅在AI生成代码无效时才介入，并从顶层开始实现。
• **Joe8756438**：认为当前理解代码的唯一方法是阅读它，不阅读代码存在风险。尽管AI可以生成代码，但阅读代码仍是最佳实践。
• **Vermon**：认为Vibe-Coding的定义就是不看代码，一旦阅读代码就不再是“氛围编码”。
• **Yanis_t**：认为依赖AI生成代码能提高生产力，最终需要放手让AI自主完成任务。
• **Kbrannigan**：将AI生成代码与早期手写汇编代码对比，认为使用AI生成代码是编程进化的自然过程。
• **_jab**：认为Vibe-Coding的效果取决于对代码样貌的清晰想象，越清晰越能快速判断AI输出是否合理。
• **Ollysb**：认为可以不阅读代码成为架构师，通过详细的前期规划和架构审查来确保代码质量。
• **Fxtentacle**：认为不阅读AI生成代码的建议是不切实际的，如同建议盲人仔细看路。
• **Chanux**：引用了Peter Naur的“编程即理论构建”文章，提供相关阅读材料以深入理解讨论。
• **Jedimastert**：对评论区中许多人愿意不经过审查就将AI生成的代码纳入代码库表示惊讶和质疑。
• **Chrisjj**：认为不审查AI生成代码会导致严重问题，并指出这种要求可能会导致不称职的程序员失去工作。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：核心争议在于是否应审查AI生成的代码。一方认为审查是确保代码质量和降低风险的必要步骤，另一方认为不阅读代码、依赖AI生成是提高生产力的途径。
• **AI的角色定位**：讨论中对AI在开发中的角色有不同看法，有人将其视为初级程序员，有人认为其仅在处理简单任务时有效，还有人认为其能大幅提升高级开发者的生产力。
• **开发流程和最佳实践**：强调遵循软件开发流程和最佳实践的重要性，反对“敏捷黑客”式的开发方式，强调代码审查、测试和验证。

总结：讨论围绕Vibe-Coding的定义、AI生成代码的审查必要性、AI在开发中的角色以及开发流程和最佳实践展开，展示了多种观点和实践经验的碰撞。

data.title: Ghost 6.0
data.author: benwerd
data.article_summary: Ghost 6.0 introduces several major upgrades, focusing on enhanced distribution and analytics. Publications are now part of an open network, allowing discovery and interaction across platforms like Bluesky, Mastodon, and Flipboard. A new native analytics suite provides real-time insights into web traffic, newsletters, and subscriptions. The platform has earned publishers over $100M in revenue, emphasizing a sustainable model based on reader support rather than ads. For developers, Ghost is transitioning to a Docker Compose environment and updating its tech stack. The update also integrates the "social web," enabling broader audience engagement and network effects for decentralized publishing, fostering direct connections with subscribers and expanding reach.

The next major version of Ghost has arrived, and our 6.0 release is packed full of more upgrades and improvements than you can shake a stick at.
If you're short on time, and you just want the highlights:
Ghost publications are now connected with an open network. People can discover, follow, like and reply to your posts across Bluesky, Flipboard, Threads, Mastodon, WordPress, Ghost, and any other social web platform. Distribution is now built-in.
We're introducing a native analytics suite for Ghost, giving you detailed insights into how your content performs across web traffic, newsletters, and member subscriptions - all in real-time, all from the same place you publish everyday.
Collectively, publishers on Ghost have now earned over
$100M
in revenue to support their work. Indie media isn't just surviving, it's thriving.
We've shipped
thousands
of improvements and updates since Ghost 5.0 that make the product more powerful than ever before.
For developers: Ghost is moving to a new official Docker Compose env, and our production stack is now Ubuntu 24, Node 22, and MySQL8.
If you want to try any of these things (and the many other improvements) go ahead and
sign up for a free trial on Ghost.org
and see for yourself. It's live now.
Or, if you want all the details about everything that's new, keep reading!
When we
announced Ghost 5.0
a few years ago, we were proud to share that Ghost's revenue had hit
$4M
– while publisher earnings had surpassed
$10M
. It felt great to have such a clear sign that our goal to create a sustainable business model for independent creators was succeeding.
Today, Ghost's annual revenue is over
$8.5M
while total publisher earnings on Ghost have now surpassed
$100M
.
While the dominant narrative in the media industry today is one of layoffs and cutbacks in a market saturated with clickbait and AI — Ghost publishers, whose revenue has grown dramatically in the past 3 years, are telling a different story.
These successful media businesses follow a simple model that's been around for a long time: They make money by directly serving readers, rather than advertisers.
After more than a decade of clickbait undermining media credibility, subscription-based publishers are discovering a simple truth: Producing high quality content that readers genuinely value is a far better business than chasing low quality page views for diminishing ad revenue.
And after more than a decade of watching questionable growth tactics from Big Tech™️ — Ghost itself proves that same simple truth when it comes to platforms. Unlike our venture-backed peers obsessed with growth at all costs, we're structured
as a non-profit foundation
that serves publishers directly with open source software.
We believe independent media cannot be beholden to proprietary tech companies, so Ghost publishers don't just "own their email list" — they own the entire software stack that underpins their business, end to end.
Not a centralized platform controlled by a single corporation, but open infrastructure that's shared by everyone.
That's the dream of the open web, and the driving force behind everything we do.
$100,000,000 later — we feel confident saying: It's working.
Grow faster, with the social web
Ghost is the home of your publication on the web, and it has always had support for multiple open distribution channels to deliver new posts to your readers.
Ghost 1.0 started with publishing by web and RSS feeds
Ghost 3.0 added support for publishing by API and webhooks
Ghost 4.0 enabled publishing by email newsletter
In Ghost 6.0 we're introducing another new distribution channel: The social web. Now, millions of people can discover, follow, like and reply to your posts from any supported social web client - including Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, Flipboard, Ghost, WordPress, Surf, WriteFreely, and many more.
Just as people can visit your Ghost website in any browser, subscribe with any feed reader, or receive newsletters in any email client, they can now follow your Ghost publication from any social web client.
Unlike closed platforms with restrictive algorithms, open web protocols create a direct connection between you and your subscribers which you have full control over.
This direct relationship has been a major driver in the resurgence of email newsletters over the past few years. But, while email is a fantastic way of sending out updates, it’s a one way street. It doesn't, and can’t, have the network effects that are so powerful for generating growth, and reaching new people.
The social web turns your Ghost publication into a networked social profile that people can find, follow, like, reply, repost and interact with from anywhere —bringing network effects directly to decentralized publishing. Popular posts can be shared, re-posted, and discussed by millions of social web users.
What does that mean, in practice?
You now have a social web reader in admin to follow and read long-form content from other Ghost, WordPress or Flipboard pub

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型的定价模式及使用者对计费方式的反应

不同观点：
• **关于计量计费的接受度：**
  - **mystraline**：消费者讨厌计量计费，尤其是当账单出乎意料时。他们宁愿为固定费用的“无限”服务多付钱，也不希望被意外收费。但如果用户能够清楚知道使用量，并能设置预算上限，计量计费是可以被接受的。
  - **ej88**：不同意文章中99%需求立即转向最新SOTA模型的说法，指出许多用户仍然选择较旧或较便宜的模型（如Sonnet 4），且很多企业用户通过API使用基于用量的计费模式。

• **关于模型的使用与定价的真实性：**
  - **furyofantares**：文章提到的某些定价模式（如Claude的200美元/月无限使用层级）实际上是有使用限制的，文章的说法可能存在误导。
  - **michaelbuckbee**：当前许多问题不需要使用SOTA模型，未来可能会看到更多由不同模型组合成的系统，以优化使用成本和效率。

• **关于模型的优化和任务分配：**
  - **johnfn**：建议创建一个能够将任务分配给“较简单”模型的智能模型，以优化资源使用。例如，Opus可以将简单任务分配给Sonnet处理。
  - **djhworld**：使用开源前端和按需付费的API模式在一开始效果不错，但当使用量增加时，费用增长非常快，用户可能没有预期到如此高的消耗。

• **关于模型使用数据的统计：**
  - **jsnell**：最高性能的模型并不一定是最多用户选择的模型。根据OpenRouter的数据，较便宜的模型（如Sonnet 4）的使用量远高于最先进的Opus 4。

• **关于AI技术的发展和商业模式：**
  - **farkin88**：虽然令牌成本在下降，但“无限”LLM计划的真正问题是用户使用曲线的极端分布。大量普通用户使用少量资源，而少数“鲸鱼用户”消耗大量资源，导致定价模式不可持续。
  - **fennecfoxy**：AI模型的商业化过于追求短期利润，可能影响了基础研究的发展。
  - **GiorgioG**：使用某些CLI工具时，费用可能出乎意料地高，导致用户不愿继续使用。

• **关于模型供应商的利润和市场策略：**
  - **ankit219**：模型构建公司可以通过更低的成本提供更好的价格，且在规模扩大的情况下，能够以更低的价格销售模型或推出有限制的“无限”计划。
  - **ktzar**：随着模型交互方式和复杂度的增加，生成有用的聊天机器人响应变得更加昂贵，用户可能被迫使用供应商的模型。

补充讨论：
- **资本和市场影响**：有评论提到硅谷文化和资本对AI技术发展的影响，特别是对快速盈利的追求可能导致研究方向的偏移。
- **技术演进和成本**：讨论中还涉及到技术发展的趋势，例如混合专家模型和外部交互，这些技术进步可能导致运行成本的增加。

data.title: Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Splatshop的工具箱，用于交互式编辑3D高斯溅射模型（Gaussian Splatting），支持选择、删除、绘制、变换等多种操作。通过一系列优化和启发式方法，Splatshop在精确编辑和实时性能之间取得了平衡，能够在包含多达1亿个基元的场景中实现高效编辑。此外，该工具还支持扩展至头戴式显示器，成为首个适用于大规模3D高斯溅射模型的VR编辑器。Splatshop旨在打造一个类似Photoshop的高斯溅射编辑工具。

44783372.article_content:
Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models
Markus Schütz, Christoph Peters, Florian Hahlbohm, Elmar Eisemann, Marcus Magnor, Michael Wimmer.
2025–06 in
Computer Graphics Forum (Proc. HPG)
44, 8.
Official version
Abstract
We present Splatshop, a highly optimized toolbox for interactive editing (selection, deletion, painting, transformation, ...) of 3D Gaussian Splatting models. Utilizing a comprehensive collection of heuristic approaches, we carefully balance between exact and fast rendering to enable precise editing without sacrificing real-time performance. Our experiments confirm that Splatshop achieves these goals for scenes with up to 100 million primitives. We also show how our proposed pipeline can be extended for use with head-mounted displays. As such, Splatshop is the first VR-capable editor for large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting models and a step towards a “Photoshop for Gaussian Splatting.”
Images
Notes
This work has been presented at HPG 2025 on June 24th. The paper has been published on June 21st.

data.title: Ultra Ethernet: Reinventing X.25
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了Broadcom新发布的ASIC芯片，据称该芯片基于新兴的超以太网规范，具有以下特点：使用优化以太网头，以10字节的会话标识符替代IP/UDP头；实现无损以太网，通过逐跳重传和错误恢复；采用基于信用的流控制（接收方实时更新发送方可用空间）。这些特性与早期的Fibre Channel、IEEE 802.1 LLC2以及X.25协议有相似之处，表明Broadcom在800 Gbps速度下重新实现了这些基本概念，再次验证了RFC 1925规则11（技术不断轮回）。

44781805.article_content:
One should never trust the technical details published by the
industry press
, but assuming the
Tomahawk Ultra puff piece
isn’t too far off the mark, the new Broadcom ASIC (supposedly loosely based on emerging Ultra Ethernet specs):
Uses
Optimized Ethernet Header
, replacing IP/UDP header with a 10-byte something (let’s call it
session identifier
)
Makes Ethernet lossless with hop-by-hop retransmission/error recovery
Uses credit-based flow control (the receiver continuously updates the sender about the amount of available space)
If you’re ancient enough, you might recognize #3 as part of Fibre Channel, #2 and #3 as part of IEEE 802.1 LLC2 (used by IBM to implement SNA over Token Ring and Ethernet), and all three as the fundamental ideas of X.25 that Broadcom obviously reinvented at 800 Gbps speeds, proving (yet again) RFC 1925 Rule 11.

   - 反对者认为该政策可能会导致逆向歧视，对没有受到政策优待的群体不公平。

data.author: oco101
data.article_summary: Demis Hassabis，谷歌DeepMind的负责人，认为人工智能（AI）将带来超越工业革命的巨大生产力和社会丰裕，但其发展速度可能快十倍。作为AI领域的先锋，Hassabis从小就是国际象棋神童，后来转向计算机和AI，创建了DeepMind。他的团队开发的AlphaFold数据库成功预测了蛋白质的结构，可能带来医学突破。然而，随着AI迅猛发展，他也对潜在风险感到担忧，希望技术巨头能放慢脚步，更好地探索未知风险。Hassabis既为AI的成就感到自豪，也意识到自己需承担解释和引导AI未来发展的责任。他认为AI将深刻影响社会，政府和公众需尽早适应和讨论这一技术。

44784717.article_content:
‘I think about the unknowns and how we can make them less unknown’ … Demis Hassabis at Google's London offices.
Photograph: Antonio Olmos/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
‘I think about the unknowns and how we can make them less unknown’ … Demis Hassabis at Google's London offices.
Photograph: Antonio Olmos/The Guardian
The G2 interview
DeepMind
Interview
Demis Hassabis on our AI future: ‘It’ll be 10 times bigger than the Industrial Revolution – and maybe 10 times faster’
Steve Rose
The head of Google’s DeepMind says artificial intelligence could usher in an era of ‘incredible productivity’ and ‘radical abundance’. But who will it benefit? And why does he wish the tech giants had moved more slowly?
Mon 4 Aug 2025 00.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 4 Aug 2025 10.40 EDT
Share
I
f you have a mental image of a Nobel prizewinner, Demis Hassabis probably doesn’t fit it. Relatively young (he’s 49), mixed race (his father is Greek-Cypriot, his mother Chinese-Singaporean), state-educated, he didn’t exactly look out of place receiving his medal from the king of Sweden in December, amid a sea of grey-haired men, but it was “very surreal”, he admits. “I’m really bad at enjoying the moment. I’ve won prizes in the past, and I’m always thinking , ‘What’s the next thing?’ But this one was really special. It’s something you dream about as a kid.”
Well, maybe not
you
, but certainly him. Hassabis was marked out as exceptional from a young age – he was a chess prodigy when he was four. Today, arguably, he’s one of the most important people in the world. As head of Google
DeepMind
, the tech giant’s artificial intelligence arm, he’s driving, if not necessarily steering, what promises to be the most significant technological revolution of our lifetimes.
As such, Hassabis finds himself in the position of being both a booster for AI and an apologist for it. The Nobel prize in chemistry was proof of the benefits AI can bring: DeepMind’s AlphaFold database was able to predict the hitherto-unfathomable structures of proteins, the building blocks of life – a breakthrough that could lead to myriad medical advances. At the same time, fears are ever growing about the AI future that
Google
is helping to usher in.
Being an AI ambassador is the part Hassabis didn’t dream about. “If I’d had my way, we would have left it in the lab for longer and done more things like AlphaFold, maybe cured cancer or something like that,” he says. “But it is what it is, and there’s some benefits to that. It’s great that everyone gets to play around with the latest AI and feel for themselves what it’s like. That’s useful for society, actually, to kind of normalise it and adapt to it, and for governments to be discussing it … I guess I have to speak up on, especially, the scientific side of how we should approach this, and think about the unknowns and how we can make them less unknown.”
In person Hassabis is a mix of down-to-earth approachability and polished professionalism. Trim and well groomed, dressed entirely in black, he wears two watches: one a smart watch, the other an analogue dress watch (smart but not too flashy). He gives the impression of someone in a hurry. We’re speaking in his office at DeepMind’s London headquarters. On the walls outside are signed chess boards from greats such as Garry Kasparov, Magnus Carlsen and Judit Polgár. He still plays; there’s a board set up on a table nearby.
View image in fullscreen
Hassabis being awarded the Nobel prize in chemistry by the king of Sweden last year.
Photograph: Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP/Getty Images
It was the chess that started Hassabis down the path of thinking about thinking. Between the ages of four and 13 he played competitively in England junior teams. “When you do that at such a young age, it’s very formative for the way your brain works. A lot of the way I think is influenced by strategic thinking from chess, and dealing with pressure.”
On paper there’s little else about Hassabis’s background that foretold his future. His family are more on the arty side: “My dad’s just finished composing a musical play in his retirement, which he staged at an arthouse theatre in north London. My sister’s a composer, so I’m kind of the outlier of the family.” They weren’t poor, but not super-wealthy. He moved between various state schools in north London, and was homeschooled for a few years.
He was also a bit of an outsider at school, he says, but he seems to have known exactly where he was going. His childhood heroes were scientific pioneers such as
Alan Turing
and
Richard Feynman
. He spent his chess winnings on early home computers such as the Sinclair ZX Spectrum and a Commodore Amiga, and learned to code. “There were few people that were interested in computers in the late 80s. There was a group of us that used to hack around, making games and other stuff, and then that became my next career after chess.”
In the 90s, the games industry was already working with AI. When he was 17, he coded the hit game

data.title: Ongoing Lean formalization of the proof for Fermat's Last Theorem
data.author: anonyonoor
data.article_summary: Imperial College London正在进行一个开源项目，旨在使用Lean定理证明器形式化费马大定理（Fermat's Last Theorem）的证明。该项目由Kevin Buzzard主导，由EPSRC资助，计划持续到2029年9月。项目采用Richard Taylor和Buzzard讨论后确定的路线，基于Wiles/Taylor-Wiles的现代变体证明。项目信息和贡献指南可在项目的GitHub页面和相关文档中找到，目前已有620个星标和88个分支。该项目托管于Imperial College London，并获得Apache-2.0许可。

• [YossarianFrPrez] 认为Lean背后的组织形式是一种新的科研 nonprofit 模式，对创业者或感兴趣于科研的人很有用，并提供了相关资源链接。这一评论更关注科研组织的创新形式，而非技术细节。

• [ants_everywhere] 对使用 Lean 进行形式化证明表示支持，但认为 Lean 在处理 quotient types 时引入了额外的公理作为一种“作弊”手段，使得从数学角度看不够完美。评论者对使用不同语言的优劣进行了比较，暗示可能存在比 Lean 更合适的语言。

• [seanwilson] 提供了有关该项目的详细概述和相关文件链接，帮助其他人了解项目背景和工作量，未对技术细节提出质疑或讨论。

• [mensetmanusman] 关心项目进展的可视化问题，询问是否存在能够展示当前进展的图形化表示，强调了项目进展透明度和可视化的重要性。

• [amelius] 提出是否可以利用 OpenAI 的 IOM 算法将现有的证明直接转换为 Lean 代码，暗示自动化工具可能加速或简化形式化过程。

• [tphyahoo2] 详细讨论了构造性数学与经典逻辑的区别，指出 Wiles 的证明依赖于矛盾证明法，并质疑 Lean 形式化过程中是否会将矛盾证明法转化为构造性证明。评论者关注形式化证明的逻辑基础及其在不同数学体系中的适应性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是使用 Lean 是否是最佳选择，特别是在处理 quotient types 时引入额外公理的做法是否合适。
• 另一个讨论点是形式化证明过程中矛盾证明法的使用及其在 Lean 中的实现方式，涉及到经典逻辑与构造性逻辑的区别。
• 自动化工具（如 OpenAI 的 IOM 算法）在形式化证明中的潜在应用也是一个讨论热点，表明技术进步可能影响未来的形式化工作流程。
• 最后，项目进展的可视化需求表明社区对项目透明度和沟通的重视。

Fermat's Last Theorem
An ongoing multi-author open source project to formalise a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in the Lean theorem prover.
Information about the project
The project is currently being led by Kevin Buzzard. Until September 2029 it is being funded by
grant EP/Y022904/1
, awarded by the EPSRC. The project is hosted at Imperial College London. Kevin would like to extend many many thanks to both of these institutions for their ongoing support of this nonstandard research.
General information ("What is Fermat's Last Theorem/Lean?" / "Why are you doing this?" etc) is
here
.
The route we will be taking was planned out essentially entirely by Richard Taylor in discussions with Buzzard. It is a modern variant of the original Wiles/Taylor-Wiles proof. For more details about the mathematics behind the proof, a good place to start is the
blueprint
.

.

44745727.article_summary: Imperial College London正在进行一个开源项目，旨在使用Lean定理证明器形式化费马大定理（Fermat's Last Theorem）的证明。该项目由Kevin Buzzard主导，由EPSRC资助，计划持续到2029年9月。项目采用Richard Taylor和Buzzard讨论后确定的路线，基于Wiles/Taylor-Wiles的现代变体证明。项目信息和贡献指南可在项目的GitHub页面和相关文档中找到，目前已有620个星标和88个分支。该项目托管于Imperial College London，并获得Apache-2.0许可。

data.title: Microsoft is open sourcing Windows 11's UI framework
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: 微软正在计划逐步开放Windows 11用户界面框架WinUI的源代码，但由于其复杂性和与操作系统专有层的关联，无法一蹴而就。微软将分阶段开放WinUI的GitHub仓库：首先增加内部提交的镜像频率，然后允许外部开发者本地构建、提交代码和运行测试，最终使GitHub成为开发和社区互动的主要平台。尽管开放过程需要时间，微软正在积极推进，同时优先考虑安全性、稳定性和现有产品支持。开发者可以通过提供反馈和提交问题来参与贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows原生UI技术的未来及相关框架的争议

不同观点：
• paavohtl认为，Windows 11用基于WebView的应用替代原生应用，导致性能下降和视觉不一致，背离了传统上操作系统开发者应展示良好性能和一致性的责任。
• arunc指出，微软以资源分配为由，将框架推给社区，但缺乏真正的善意和长期支持，暗示微软不负责任。
• pjmlp表示，Windows开发社区对WinUI不感兴趣，特别是那些因Windows 8以来多次失败而失望的开发者，认为微软不会解决现有问题。
• muhehe认为，Windows的UI框架繁多且混乱，质疑开源是否真的对开发者有实际好处，还是仅为了表现开放。
• tekdude支持继续开发WPF，认为其具有一定的优势和改进潜力，如编译时代码生成和性能提升，但担忧时间和资源投入问题。

补充讨论：
• LarMachinarum提到，不仅是Windows，跨平台和开源UI框架也存在问题，如GTK的混乱和Qt的许可模式，认为目前缺少一个好的跨平台原生UI框架。
• daemin批评WinUI3的开发体验差，调试麻烦且示例程序崩溃，因此继续使用Win32和WTL。
• Springtime希望Windows 11引入原生垂直任务栏功能，目前依赖第三方工具实现。
• chiph怀念过去微软提供的UI开发支持，认为现代工具缺乏帮助开发者创建与系统无缝集成的应用。
• bob1029偏好使用Win32/GDI/DirectDraw等低级API，认为这些API稳定且不易被微软改变。
• BoorishBears幽默地指出，Windows拥有众多UI框架且各有缺陷，没有明确赢家。
• bobajeff质疑微软为何不直接采用Electron/TypeScript作为Windows UI框架，特别是微软已经拥有GitHub和vscode。
• dehrmann认为，Windows市场份额下降，微软可能对整个Windows平台的投入减少，用户转向其他设备。
• eska提到，单个开发者能通过学习OS和WinAPI创建高性能原生UI，暗示微软应更注重原生开发。
• AraceliHarker认为，微软对WinUI失去兴趣，意图用WebView替代，开源仅是形式。

争议焦点：
• 微软是否对Windows原生UI技术（如WinUI）失去兴趣，转向基于Web的技术。
• 开源框架是否真正对开发者有益，还是仅为微软的战略转移手段。
• Windows平台的未来发展方向及微软的长期投入承诺。

44765600.article_content:
Microsoft has plenty of open-source projects, and these days, the company is much more open to community contributions. Still, plenty of code remains closed-source, and the company constantly receives more requests to open it. One of them is WinUI, Windows 11's user interface framework. While Microsoft is not opening it fully yet, the company shared details about plans for the next six months, which include "product work and foundational changes to support a more open and collaborative future."
Microsoft
says
that open-sourcing WinUI cannot be done with a switch flip due to its complexity and connections. Windows 11's user interface taps into many proprietary layers of the operating system that cannot be published as is. As such, Microsoft needs to separate what could be shared with the community and what cannot.
Many of you have asked about truly open sourcing the repo. While we’re not ready to commit to a specific end date for completing all milestones, we are actively working toward it. This isn’t a flip-the-switch moment, it’s a deliberate process.
Additionally, the team needs to prioritize other things, which include security, stability, and support for existing products.
Microsoft plans to open WinUI's GitHub repository in phases:
Phase 1: Increased Mirror Frequency
. After the WASDK 1.8 release (end of August), we’ll begin more frequent mirroring of internal commits to GitHub to increase transparency and show progress.
Phase 2: 3rd Party Devs Build Locally
. External developers will be able to clone and build the repo locally, with documentation to guide setup and dependencies.
Phase 3: 3rd Party Devs Contribute & Run Tests
. Contributors will be able to submit PRs and run tests locally. We’re working to untangle private dependencies and make test infrastructure publicly accessible.
Phase 4: GitHub as Center of Gravity
. GitHub becomes the primary place for development, issue tracking, and community engagement. Internal mirrors will be phased out.
Making WinUI more open will be an incremental process, and you can track it on
this board on GitHub
. Meanwhile, developers can contribute by sharing their feedback, filing clear and well-written issues, and upvoting existing feedback.

data.title: Remote hosting for your telescope
data.author: gregorvand
data.article_summary: Sierra Remote Observatories (SRO) 提供位于内华达山脉的顶级望远镜 hosting 服务，自2007年起运营，目前有超过174台望远镜。该地点具备卓越的天文观测条件，夏季视宁度1角秒，冬季1.2角秒，峰值可达亚角秒级，每年290个晴夜，黑暗程度21.80 Mag/ArcSec²，平均风速1英里/小时，无夏季季风。基础设施包括24/7技术支持、光纤互联网（1 Gbps，可升级至更高速度）、现场机械修理服务、Starlink备份网络等。提供每月2小时免费技术支持，并可协助安装望远镜。租用价格从每月600美元起，也提供如iTelescope等可租用望远镜选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程天文台托管服务及其相关话题

不同观点：
• [支持观点] tbagman 推荐了 StarFront Observatories，认为其地理位置优越， skies 条件好，且采用了高密度托管模式，降低了成本，吸引了大量深空天文摄影爱好者。此外，还提到偶尔会有协作项目，提供了更多互动机会。
• [应用场景扩展] fudged71 提出了远程托管模型是否适用于其他非计算领域的疑问，例如3D打印农场，显示出对该模式广泛应用的兴趣。
• [成本质疑] michaeldoron 对所谓的“免费”技术支持提出质疑，指出技术支持实际上是包含在600美元/月的费用中的，属于文字游戏。
• [家庭教育需求] jalk 表达了希望带孩子体验天文观测的愿望，但由于旅行和夜间时间的限制，寻找在线服务（提供导览和“动手”望远镜控制）未果，显示了对用户友好型服务的需求。
• [惊喜发现] teddy-smith 表示对远程天文台托管服务的存在感到高兴，显示出对新技术和体验的开放态度。
• [体验质疑] _xerces_ 对远程服务持怀疑态度，认为这剥夺了人们亲身接触星空和学习天文学的乐趣，质疑其对传统天文爱好的影响。
• [共享经济模式] RainyDayTmrw 提出了时间共享模式的可能性，认为可以多人共享一个望远镜的使用时间，显示出对经济可行性的关注。
• [其他服务推荐] incognito124 提到了另一个位于西班牙的远程望远镜托管服务，提供了更多选择。
• [商业模式赞赏] ge96 提到了YouTube上有人建立了远程操作望远镜的牧场，认为这是一个很酷的商业模式，显示出对创新商业模式的认可。
• [成本敏感] yapyap 认为600美元/月的价格对普通人来说过高，建议普通收入人群更倾向于在自己后院托管望远镜，显示出对成本的敏感性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了多个远程望远镜托管服务的例子，包括StarFront Observatories和Pixelskies Astro，显示出这一市场的多样性和国际化。
• 对远程天文台服务的不同态度反映了传统天文爱好与现代科技结合的争议，尤其是亲身体验与便捷性之间的平衡。
• 对成本的讨论显示出不同收入群体对远程托管服务的接受度差异，以及对经济可行性的关注。

• [其他服务推荐] incognito124 提到了另一个位于西班牙的远程望远镜托管服务，提供了更多选择。

data.author: veqq

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（尤其是大型语言模型）在历史叙述、翻译等领域的作用及其潜在风险

不同观点：
• munificent：认为历史是不断重新诠释的过程，LLM无法做到这一点。科技公司试图用LLM替代这些工作，以控制叙事和世界。
• dale_glass：最大的风险不是AI替代历史学家或翻译，而是我们会被说服不需要他们。AI替代低需求的重复性工作，可能导致这些领域失去存在的基础。
• krunck：AI导致信息集中到少数几个来源，历史解释不应由与强权政府结盟的少数实体控制。
• masfuerte：AI可以大大缩短初步翻译草案的时间，但对打磨和精细翻译的作用有限。
• Phui3ferubus：翻译被ML/AI取代是因为公司不重视质量，只关注成本。
• moritzwarhier：对AI的讨论常缺乏深入思考，AI与互联网的结合让人联想到1984年的情景。
• Obscurity4340：同意历史无法客观，LLM无法进行再诠释和三角测量。
• vouaobrasil：目前LLM无法完全替代人类翻译，但它们使翻译工作变得不那么繁琐。如果翻译变得过于容易，可能会导致平庸作品的增加。
• pavel_lishin：机器翻译在传达语气、讽刺和文化暗示方面存在缺陷，导致翻译质量低下。
• foxglacier：文章误解了微软的“AI适用性评分”，该评分并不等同于工作被AI替代的风险。高需求可能导致翻译工作增加。
• NitpickLawyer：反对将LLM称为“平均机器”，指出这些模型在国际数学奥林匹克中获得金奖，表现优异。
• glenstein：同意事实带有隐含的认识论，但认为这并不导致极端相对主义。好的理论可以具有弹性和责任感，AI目前的不足在于缺乏人类直觉和文化好奇心，但这不意味着AI永远无法达到人类理解的水平。

补充讨论：
• AI在历史和翻译领域的应用可能导致信息集中化和低质量作品增加。
• 对AI的过度依赖可能使我们忽视人类工作的独特价值。
• 有人认为AI最终可能突破目前的限制，因此不应过早下定论。
• 对AI适用性评分的误解可能导致对AI替代人类工作的错误判断。
• AI在某些领域表现出色，但目前仍无法完全替代人类在复杂诠释任务中的作用。

data.title: I Asked Four Former Friends Why We Stopped Speaking-Here's What I Learned (2023)
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在28岁时对友谊的反思和困惑。作者与最亲密的朋友Simone因生活变化而逐渐疏远，同时在搬到肯尼亚后，也难以融入当地社交圈，感到孤独和不安。作者试图通过与过去的朋友对话，了解友谊破裂的原因，但大部分人无法理解她的困境。文章探讨了人在20多岁时因生活转变、恋爱关系和优先级变化而失去朋友的普遍现象，并表达了缺乏友谊的孤独感和对自我价值的怀疑。作者最终决定通过直接对话 former friends，寻找答案和解决办法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章中关于人际关系变淡、友谊结束及其原因的分析

不同观点：
• [avereveard] 认为文章缺乏结论，且最后的讨论方向（“是否应该和前任朋友交谈”）不适合他的情况。他指出了几种关系变淡的可能原因，包括缺乏共同努力、价值观分歧、误解、地理距离和情感疏离。
• [glxxyz] 没有直接评论文章内容，只是提供了一个存档链接。
• [mmmlinux] 简短指出，人会改变，且地理上的变动（如搬到肯尼亚）是关系变化的一个因素。
• [readthenotes1] 认为文章本可以成为自我中心的关注寻求帖，但实际上聚焦于关系渐行渐远时不同人的视角，这点值得肯定。
• [rado] 总结了文章中的几个学习点，包括成年人友谊的丧失常与生活转变有关，直接沟通有助于理解关系结束的原因，个人成长来自于对自身问题的认识，而不仅仅是责备或后悔，重连不代表关系一定会恢复。
• [rendall] 对文章中的描述方式提出质疑，认为文章中的人物对话不自然，与现实生活中人们的描述方式不符。他指出文章中的描述过于戏剧化，不符合实际交流的习惯。
• [rambojohnson] 认为文章是无聊的自恋式内省，且对文章的写作方向不满意，预期文章会讨论朋友群体的疏远，结果并没有让他感到意外。

补充讨论：
• 文章的结论和目标读者存在争议。一些评论者（如 avereveard 和 rambojohnson）认为文章的结论不明确或不适合他们的情况。
• 人际关系变淡的原因有多种，包括地理距离、价值观分歧、误解等，这些是评论中反复提到的因素。
• 文章的写作风格和描述的真实性受到质疑，尤其是 rendall 的评论，指出文章中的对话和描述不符合现实生活中的交流习惯。
• 个人成长与关系结束的关系是 rado 评论中的一个亮点，强调了自我反省在关系结束中的价值，而不仅仅是试图恢复关系。

On a warm July evening, I dove into bed and grabbed my phone, giddy and anxious. As I scrolled through TikTok, attempting to calm my nerves, a Google Calendar notification flashed on the screen: “VIDEO CALL WITH SIMONE.”
Before I could swipe the reminder away, Simone FaceTimed me. I attempted to rehearse my greeting as the call buffered:
Should I keep it cool with a, “Hey, what’s good?” No, that sounds cold. What about a Keke Palmer-esque, “Girl!” No, that’s doing too much. “Good evening?” No, it’s not evening her time, that doesn’t even make sen—
“Girl!” Simone said with a chuckle.
I couldn’t help but crack a smile. As I’d learned over the course of our six-year friendship, her warmth never failed to replace my anxiety with joy.
“Damn, it’s been a
minute
.” she added.
She was right. Though Simone is my closest friend, we don’t see or talk to each other often. Both are my fault. In 2020, after months holed up in my tiny Washington, D.C. apartment, I decided to wait out the winter at my mother’s cottage in Kenya. It was just what the doctor ordered, and a few months later, I decided to move to Nairobi permanently.
My move changed our friendship—it changed
all
of my friendships, actually. I tried to stay in touch with my friends stateside for a while, but as time went on, FaceTime dates became harder to plan, and fewer voice notes were exchanged via WhatsApp. Now, I don’t know if I can call any of them friends anymore—and my relationship with Simone felt like it was hanging by a thread.
Things in Kenya aren’t much better. Though I’m Kenyan by ethnicity, I grew up abroad, in the US and UK, and I’ve found that my foreign accent and perspective other me, even within my family. These days, my social life tends to begin and end with nights on the couch, re-watching
Shameless
with my boyfriend. I’m ashamed and terrified about that reality; it feels dangerous to rely on only him for human connection.
After all, friends are witnesses to your life. They enrich the living experience. Not having that makes me feel like that tree that falls in the forest alone: Can anybody hear me? Do I matter?
Marriage and family therapist Shontel Cargill promises me that these feelings are normal. She says that friendship loss in one’s mid-to-late 20s is common for several reasons: life transitions, romantic relationships, evolution of priorities, and more. And while it doesn’t happen to everyone, for some, friendship loss “can lead to psychological distress,” sparking issues with anxiety, depression, trust, and self-esteem.
Check, check, check, and check.
Cargill says that talking about your struggles with others can help the healing process, but I’ll be honest—that hasn’t worked for me. Most people I’ve spoken to about my predicament don’t get it, which only makes me feel worse. I tried to bring it up on my aforementioned call with Simone, but her empathetic smile and pitying eyes said it all: She couldn’t relate. Lucky her.
I needed answers. Concrete ones—not those generic suggestions that I “put myself out there” or “just give it time.” Everyone around me had managed to hold on to friends throughout their lives; everyone seemed to be on girls’ trips and boozy brunches; seemed to have a tribe of confidants ready to drop everything for them. And here I was, a lonely, overworked 28-year-old who spent way too much time in her apartment, wondering why she didn’t have any of that.
So, like a good journalist, I decided to investigate. After speaking to Simone, I determined that I’d reach out to some of my former friends directly, and see if we could have a conversation about why we “broke up.” Many declined, and understandably so. But to my surprise, a few agreed to participate in my crazy scheme.
Here are those conversations—and their revelations. Their names have been changed.
Celine
Circumstance brought Celine and me together. We were both new freshmen at an international school in Nairobi, and our shared fear proved the perfect BFF elixir. Celine was sweet and reserved, with a quiet confidence that I admired—even more so when I got older. But she wanted to do her own thing and I, a not-so-confident 14-year-old, wanted to fit in. I had a hunger for popularity, and when I realized that Celine didn’t share that, I neglected the friendship. Soon, it evaporated.
Celine remembered things similarly.
“Once school started, we new kids were initially welcomed into the group of ‘misfits’ that every high school has,” she wrote to me via Facebook. “But eventually, we broke away—you, to join the funny kids, a group of hilarious and friendly people who could match your unparalleled wit and high-octane energy and me, to join the kids at the back of the bus, literally and figuratively.”

data.title: Show HN: I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
data.author: benholmen
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者花费六年时间打造了一个不实用的1000像素木制显示屏，名为"Kilopixel"。该项目灵感来源于一些非传统艺术作品和低帧率的电子墨水屏播放器，旨在创建一个任何人都能通过网页互动的低效显示器。显示屏采用40x25的像素网格，每个像素通过单一机制逐一旋转，与现代显示器相比效率极低。

作者首先尝试使用木制结构和各种材料作为像素，包括乒乓球、泡沫球、木球等，但由于成本、重量和易碎性等问题均未成功。最终，在2024年，通过与他人讨论，作者决定放弃球形像素，改为使用立方体像素。

项目涉及网络应用、物理控制器、定制CNC构建、3D建模和打印等多方面技术，是作者迄今为止最雄心勃勃的项目。读者可以通过kilopx.com亲自体验这个独特的显示屏。

44787902.article_content:
I spent 6 years building a ridiculous wooden pixel display
August 2, 2025
TL,DR: I built the world's most impractical 1000-pixel display and anyone in the world can draw on it
If you just want to play with it, goto
kilopx.com
.
The backstory
Six years ago I had an idea to build a large, inefficient display with a web interface that anyone could interact with. I've enjoyed
Danny Rozin's unconvenional mirrors
over the years and was inspired by an
eInk movie player that played at 24 frames per
hour
that got me thinking about a laborious display that could slowly assemble an image.
I landed on the idea of a 40Ã25 pixel grid of pixels, turned one by one by a single mechanism. Compared to our modern displays with millions of pixels changing 60 times a second, a wooden display that changes a single pixel 10 times a
minute
is an incredibly inefficient way to create an image. Conveniently, 40Ã25 = 1,000 pixels, leading to the name
Kilopixel
and the six-letter domain name
kilopx.com
. How do you back down from that? That's the best domain name I've ever owned.
So I got to work. This project has everything: a web app, a physical controller, a custom CNC build, generated gcode, tons of fabrication, 3d modeling, 3d printing, material sourcing - so much to get lost in. It's the most ambitious project I've ever built.
The first prototype: 21Ã3 pixels
My first thought was to use a wooden gantry that would ride on some sort of track. Since I'm most comfortable working with wood, it's my default prototyping medium. However, I quickly pivoted to extruded aluminum and the excellent
hardware kits from Openbuilds
that include pulleys, gantry parts, extruded aluminum, and timing belts. It's very similar to the materials used in 3D printer frames, and connects very easily with off the shelf stepper motors. This allowed me to build a gantry with X and Y, essentially a wall-mounted XY plotter. I built the first prototype with two stepper motors, a Raspberry Pi, a CNC controller, and a beefy power supply. It allowed me to generating and sending instructions to the CNC controller to move to a particular pixel, turning that pixel, and reading values from sensors. It also revealed quite a few problems with my pixel choices and pixel manipulation mechanisms.
1,000 of anything is
expensive
Picking pixels was a real adventure. I've tried ping pong balls, styrofoam balls, bouncy balls, wooden balls, 3d printed balls, golf balls, foam balls...anything approximately spherical and about 1-1.5in in diameter. The problems I encountered were largely cost (even a 50Â¢ ball is $500 of balls), weight (again, a thousand of these things), and availability. For a long time I thought ping pong balls were my best bet, so I purchased a few hundred of them, 3d printed painting jigs, and spray painted them. I used a hot nail to melt two opposite holes on each ball so they could be strung up on the display.
Ping pong balls are basically soda cans
You can stand on a soda can,
as long as it's not open
. Open the can, and it crushes easily. Ping pong balls are the same way. They're relatively strong until you melt two holes in them. Then they can be deformed, which is fatal to any spray paint you've put on them. And not only are they fragile, but the cheap ones are inconsistently sized, and a half millimeter here and there adds up when you have a row of 40 balls. Ping pong balls were a no-go.
Nerfed
My next attempt at a cheap, spherical pixel was foam Nerf balls - much smaller than ping pong balls, and only available in bright colors. They accepted spray paint OK but the paint deteriorated over time.
It was difficult to consistently bore a hole through the nerf balls, and they really liked to grab the wire and were hard to turn. I struggled to consistently turn them and I wasn't thrilled with the bright colors.
I also tried bouncy balls (hard to drill a hole, hard to paint, inconsistent sizes, heavy), wooden balls (not very round, hard to paint a crisp line, heavy), and styrofoam balls (hard to paint with acrylic paint, and they melt with spray paint).
Turning balls
I had the idea to use a small, slow motor to rotate a LEGO wheel against the ping pong ball. I'd use a reflectivity sensor to detect if it was showing black or white, and stop once the pixel was rotated properly. I modeled and printed a custom hub for a LEGO wheel, a few different mechanisms to move the wheel in and out of contact of the sphere, and an interface for the gantry. I tried using a solenoid to push the motor into the ball, which was underpowered, and a servo. Neither approach worked great and ultimately I decided this ball turning approach was a dead end.
Pivoting to non-spherical pixels
In 2024 I had a couple of productive conversations with
Joe Tannenbaum on the Side Project podcast
and
Chris Morrell on the Over Engineered podcast
. Those conversations helped me consider that maybe balls were not the way to go - I thought about flaps and illuminated buttons, then settled on a cubic

data.title: Gigabyte removes PCIe 5.0 support from B650 motherboards in latest BIOS update
data.author: josephcsible
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：B650主板对PCIe 5.0支持的问题及相关消费者反应

不同观点：
• Aurornis认为，B650主板从未正式支持GPU插槽的PCIe 5.0，只有B650E主板才支持。他解释说，M.2插槽和扩展插槽在规格上存在区别，B650主板的设计和测试都是基于PCIe 4.0的预期，如果强行启用PCIe 5.0可能会导致不稳定和系统崩溃，增加退货率和顾客不满。

• Amatecha表达了对购买的主板被宣传支持PCIe 5.0但实际仅限于M.2插槽的困惑和不满。他提到自己刚购买的电脑明确标示支持PCIe 5.0，但现在意识到仅限于存储而非GPU插槽，并表示会继续使用当前BIOS版本以避免问题。

• Toast0指出，类似的情形在AM4平台上也曾发生过，暗示这种情况可能是厂商更新或调整产品特性的一部分，而非个例。

• Josephcsible提出，厂商不应在售后收回已售产品的功能，即使该功能存在bug或未被正式宣传。他认为这种做法应被视为非法。

• Oakwhiz从技术角度提出疑问，认为可能是信号完整性问题导致无法支持PCIe 5.0，暗示硬件设计上的限制可能是根本原因。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于消费者对产品功能预期的落差以及厂商是否应在售后取消或调整产品特性。
• 部分用户对产品规格的理解存在混淆，特别是M.2插槽和GPU插槽在PCIe支持上的不同。
• 有人提出这种现象并非首次发生，可能与硬件设计和测试的局限性有关。
• 法律和消费者权益问题也被提及，特别是产品功能被“收回”是否合理。

• **与其他体验的联想**：[512] 提到该平台让他想起Optiver实习生选拔过程，暗示平台可能具备某种教育和筛选的功能。

• **类似产品的推荐**：[2kblater] 分享了自己为孩子制作的类似游戏，适合3至5岁儿童，并提供了Steam链接。

• **对孩子使用情况的询问**：[pizzathyme] 询问平台创建者的孩子年龄以及他们是否喜欢这些益智游戏。

• **浏览器兼容性问题**：[jacobmarble] 报告了使用Firefox浏览器访问平台时遇到的SSL连接错误问题。

• **对直接链接功能的建议**：[ArekDymalski] 建议为每个游戏提供直接URL链接，以便用户可以更方便地分享和引导孩子参与特定题目。

• **游戏体验中的具体问题**：[jamoner] 提到在玩一个求和游戏时，无法找到三个数相加等于15的组合，并表示可以提供截图以帮助解决问题。

补充讨论：
• **对平台整体的正面评价**：[nickpsecurity] 简单表示了对平台的赞赏，特别是为其孩子打造的用心设计。

争议焦点：
• 游戏生成算法的问题：[getnormality] 指出的题目生成不准确问题与其他用户对游戏内容的正面评价形成对比，表明平台在题目生成算法上可能存在改进空间。

• 浏览器兼容性问题：[jacobmarble] 提出的Firefox浏览器无法访问平台的问题，提示平台在兼容性方面需要进一步测试和优化。

不同观点：
• [flipnotyk] 认为Lidar地图数据通常需要经过后期处理和调整，才能精确地对齐到客户要求的具体位置。他以自己的工作经验为例，强调了数据修正的必要性，并对可能在这张地图上付出细致工作的人表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 地图的准确性存在局部差异：[lemonberry] 的反馈显示，尽管地图在某些方面（如街道名称）存在错误，但在其他细节（如石墙）上却表现准确。

data.title: Drawafish.com Postmortem: Whoops
data.author: hallak
data.article_summary: DrawAFish.com 网站经历了一次约6小时的安全事件，期间用户名被恶意篡改为侮辱性词汇，不当的鱼图被批准，正常的鱼图被删除。根本原因包括：遗留的6位管理员密码在过去的数据泄露中被曝光，用户名更新API缺乏身份验证，以及JWT未绑定到特定用户。事件发生后，通过手动恢复管理操作、修复授权逻辑并审查备份来解决问题。此次事件源于作者的快速开发（“vibe-coding”）和多个安全漏洞，如暴露的旧密码和未认证的API。最终，在社区帮助下，问题得以解决，作者从中吸取了教训，强调了高速度开发中的风险。

44784743.article_content:
DrawAFish.com
TL;DR:
Incident Duration:
~6 hours (2AM–8AM EST)
Impact:
Username vandalism (slurs)
Offensive fish approved / safe fish removed
Root Causes:
Legacy 6-digit admin password exposed in past data breach
Username update API lacked authentication
JWT not tied to specific user
Mitigation:
Manual reversal of mod actions, fixed authorization logic, backups reviewed
Takeaway:
hwoopsy daisy 🙂
Did you see? Did you see it? What it says? What it says on top of the website?
If you were on HackerNews on
Aug 1 2025
, you may have seen
DrawAFish.com
.
Because it was in the number 1 spot. You also may have seen it if you follow me on
instagram
. You also probably saw
that I was in the #1 spot on Hackernews there too. Because I posted about it a lot. And also if you
talked to me in person you probably heard about it. And then you probably heard a lot of quotes from
The Social Network
(2010) where I replaced various words with "Fish."
"A million fish isn't cool. You know what's cool?
A billion fish
."
If you read the post on Hackernews, you saw that the website was an exercise in
vibe-coding. I used Copilot to implement features, and I used it to implement features
fast
.
In my career,
[0]
I have learned the art of "Blameless
Postmortems." The problem with a Blameless
Postmortem is that it doesn't really work when you're the sole contributor. So this is a blameful
postmortem. And I blame me. (Not the LLM, sorry).
If you saw the website only on August 1, you probably do not understand why I need to write a postmortem
at
all. Everything went swimmingly (ha, ha). But if you had the displeasure of viewing my website between
the hours of 2AM (20 minutes after I went to sleep) and 8AM (when I woke up)
[1]
EST on Aug 3, then you would have seen chaos. Every single username was
transformed to a heinous slur, many unsavory fish had made it into the fishtank, and many beautiful fish
were gone. How did this happen?
The Vulnerabilities
This is not what they changed my username to. I'll let you use your
imagination.
Legacy admin password exposed in data breach:
When creating the website, I used
my childhood username and my childhood 6-digit password for testing. I think the first time it
leaked was on Neopets.com.
[2]
I then set up
Google Auth. From then on, I only logged in with Google Auth. But the password remained. I
simply forgot. This allowed some of the most intelligent and brilliant minds on the internet to
find my password on the Neopets data leak paste, log in as an admin, and approve and disapprove
some really disgusting and horrible fish.
On the plus side, the brilliant minds (while attempting to ban every single user) managed to
accidentally ban themselves. So that vulnerability was only an active issue for an hour or so.
Username update API lacked authentication:
I vibe coded the profile backend,
which allows users to modify their username. I added this feature last minute, figured I'd
review it later, and then didn't. The username modification did not perform any auth logic
whatsoever. whoopsy
JWT not tied to specific user:
There was another security vulnerability - I
used the JWT to authorize login, but never confirmed that the JWT token belonged to the userId /
email associated with it in the admin actions. So you could log in with my username and password,
grab the JWT, and then send that along with your request. While this was a mistake, it ended up
saving me. Fortunately, hackernews user @
iceweaselfan44
used this vulnerability to authorize as an admin and
delete the really bad fish. He was awake, on the other side of the world, removing fish and
helping out.
[3]
The Recovery
Moderation logs. There are so many of these.
I woke up at around 7:45 am, saw a couple pings and messages, and immediately rushed to my desktop.
[4]
Fortunately, I had set up firebase backups.
Unfortunately, I had set them up wrong. I spent a good hour or so diagnosing the errors and then quickly
pushed changes to require authentication.
I had a mod log set up, so undoing the changes was as simple as writing an annoying script that just
undid all the mod actions. Did I learn my lesson about vibe coding? Maybe. I vibe coded the script,
looked over the code, and did a dry run first.
I banned the other mod account ran by IceWeasel
[5]
and
patched the JWT bug - at which point he reached out to me and explained how he created it. We then
hopped on a call and he took a look at the codebase, where he expertly suggested a refactor that would
be more idiomatic with current security practices. And then when I blindly pushed it and it broke
everything, he expertly committed some more changes that fixed it.
Reflection
At this point, you're probably thinking: geeze man. Wow. youve gotta be stupid.
And I'd like to get on my hands and knees and beg for your suspension of belief when I say: yes I am but
not when it comes to my job. It is really fun to just have high velocity, and it is really fun to not do
code reviews and to just push stuff. Sometime

data.title: Customizing tmux and making it less dreadful
data.author: EPendragon
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了终端复用工具 **tmux** 的功能和使用体验。tmux 允许在一个终端中运行多个终端会话，支持创建多个窗口和窗格，便于同时处理多个任务。其主要功能包括保护远程服务器上的运行程序、从不同设备访问远程会话以及灵活的会话管理（如分离和重连）。尽管初始界面不友好且快捷键复杂，但 tmux 高度可定制，用户可以通过编辑 `.tmux.conf` 文件自定义快捷键和外观。例如，更改默认前缀键 `C-b` 为 `C-a`，以及设置分屏和切换窗格的快捷键。文章还提到使用 **iTerm2**、**Powerline10k** 和 **NerdFonts** 可以增强 tmux 的视觉效果。总体而言，tmux 功能强大，但需要一定的学习成本。

• Oh my tmux作为一个配置框架，可能为tmux用户提供了更丰富的自定义选项和功能增强，但需要用户投入时间进行设置和调整。

评论中主要对比了Zellij和tmux（及其配置框架Oh my tmux）的使用体验，讨论了工具的易用性和自定义能力，反映了不同用户对终端复用工具的不同需求和偏好。

44787374.article_content:
I have been exploring some new tools here and there. When I started watching
Primeagen
, I took a note of several tools that he was using and advocating for. One of them was tmux.
What is tmux?
#
tmux
is a terminal multiplexer. What that means is you can have many terminals in one. According to tmux wiki:
tmux is a program which runs in a terminal and allows multiple other terminal programs to be run inside it. Each program inside tmux gets its own terminal managed by tmux, which can be accessed from the single terminal where tmux is running - this called multiplexing and tmux is a terminal multiplexer.
tmux goes further by allowing you to have a lot of control over how the terminals are displayed, how they function, and how are they styled. You can have many separate windows as tabs. You can have many panes within one window. Are you working on several different projects? Then why don’t you have multiple sessions - each of them containing sets of windows and panes - all giving you access to multiple terminals. With a tool like this you no longer need to arrange multiple terminal instance windows on your desktop or using multiple workspaces for those instances - you can have it all in one place.
One additional feature that tmux boasts in is the ability to retain the terminal session upon its closure. Imagine that you have a long running process like a local server or a persistent connection like ssh session. If you were to close that window, you would lose that session and the process that was in it. Tmux has the ability to detach and attach to multiple sessions making them easier to manage and not to worry about losing it.
tmux wiki goes into detail talking about several other features of tmux:
The main uses of tmux are to:
Protect running programs on a remote server from connection drops by running them inside tmux.
Allow programs running on a remote server to be accessed from multiple different local computers.
Work with multiple programs and shells together in one terminal, a bit like a window manager.
For example:
A user connects to a remote server using ssh(1) from an xterm(1) on their work computer and run several programs. perhaps an editor, a compiler and a few shells.
They work with these programs interactively, perhaps start compiling, then close the xterm(1) with tmux and go home for the day.
They are then able to connect to the same remote server from home, attach to tmux, and continue from where they were previously.
My first tmux experience
#
The first impression of tmux didn’t leave me with much excitement of exploring what is truly possible :/ Source:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Getting-Started
When I first started using tmux, I felt overwhelmed by the very poor default UI that it offers and the amount of options and shortcuts that I needed to know to operate it well and be productive. It took me several tries before I started to feel more or less comfortable with it.
One of the things that stood out to me right away was how dreadful UI looked. Not only it felt uninviting, but it almost felt “gatekeepy” - if you don’t know how to use it in this configuration, then might as well forget about it. But one thing that kept me going was the promise of a highly customizable terminal that I could make my own at some point.
While promising all of these amazing features, the dreadful tmux UI didn’t necessarily inspire :( Source:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Getting-Started
Customization journey
#
To preface, I must mention that I am using
iterm2
with
Powerline10k
and
NerdFonts
. They heavily affect the final look of the tmux due to colors and icons being inherited from the iterm2 configuration. With that said, let’s get into it.
The file that is responsible for customizing tmux - its function and its look - is
.tmux.conf
. This file should be located in user’s Home folder a.k.a.
~/
. That is where tmux will be looking for it.
There are quite a few options when it comes to customizing tmux. One of the first things that I wanted to address was the
prefix
key binding. This prefix is a key combination that you would use to enter the tmux shortcut or command mode. By default, the prefix is
C-b
a.k.a.
Ctrl-b
. One of the common remaps that most people go with is to switch it to
C-a
, which is a lot easier to use. To do that, we need to add the following lines to the configuration file:
# remap prefix from 'C-b' to 'C-a'
unbind C-b
set-option -g prefix C-a
bind-key C-a send-prefix
While researching ways to customize tmux, I stumbled upon several more useful key remaps, which I decided to use:
# split panes using | and -
bind
|
split-window -h
bind
- split-window -v
unbind
'"'
unbind %
# reload config file (change file location to your the tmux.conf you want to use)
bind
r source-file ~/.tmux.conf
;
display-message
"~/.tmux.conf reloaded."
# switch panes using Alt-arrow without prefix
bind
-n M-Left
select
-pane -L
bind
-n M-Right
select
-pane -R
bind
-n M-Up
select
-pane -U
bind
-n M-Down
select

data.title: Show HN: Mathpad – Physical keypad for typing 100+ math symbols anywhere
data.author: MagneLauritzen
data.article_summary: Mathpad是一款专为简化数学符号输入而设计的键盘，解决了输入数学符号繁琐的问题。它配备了120个数学符号和希腊字母，支持LaTeX、Microsoft Office和LibreOffice等多种输出格式，适用于Windows、macOS和Linux系统。Mathpad采用Gateron KS-33热插拔机械开关，整个设备开源且可定制。项目已完成开发，正在众筹中，计划在活动结束后开始生产并交付。需要注意的是，它仅支持拉丁字母键盘布局，且在Windows系统上需要运行一个小应用程序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mathpad项目的功能、设计选择及其实用性

不同观点：
• [积极支持] toomuchtodo认为该项目非常酷，并表示会捐款支持，赞赏了设计者投入的心思。tonetegeatinst也表达了对项目的赞赏，并表示在未来有需求时会购买。
• [功能疑问] staplung对Mathpad的希腊字母输入方式有疑问，特别是如何输入大写希腊字母，如∆（delta），并询问是否需要结合常规键盘的Shift键使用。
• [设计质疑] olejorgenb对使用交错布局表示不解，质疑这种设计是否必要，指出数字键盘并非交错布局但人们仍能轻松使用。
• [实用性比较] westurner对Mathpad的效率提出质疑，比较了Mathpad与使用Unicode或LaTeX表格的效率，询问Mathpad在速度上的具体优势。

补充讨论：
• toomuchtodo提到Elgato Stream Deck作为一种可能的选择，暗示这种设备可能也能满足类似需求，询问设计者是否考虑过这种替代方案。

What if Mathematical Symbols Were as Easy to Type as Regular Letters?
After 3 years of development, Mathpad finally makes this dream a reality. Anyone who’s struggled to type equations knows the pain: When you need symbols beyond basic arithmetic, you’re forced to hunt for them—copy-pasting from the web, digging through clunky symbol pickers, or memorizing obscure alt-codes. Mathpad fixes this. Just press a key, and the symbol appears instantly.

data.title: Every Visual Workflow Tool Is Just Excel for Developers Who Gave Up
data.author: dalibenothmen
data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了视觉工作流工具（如Zapier、Microsoft Power Automate等）实质上是“放弃开发的开发者的Excel”。这些工具看似简化了复杂逻辑的构建，但实际上创造了难以调试的依赖网络，使问题更难解决。作者指出，这些工具的成功并非因为它们更优秀，而是因为开发者变得懒惰和害怕，产生了自我怀疑，并试图避免做大量决策。此外，这些工具通过订阅模式限制用户能力，收取高额费用，使用户在经济和功能上受限。作者呼吁开发者重新审视这些工具的真实价值，并质疑为 inferior 工具付费的合理性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Excel及可视化工作流工具的优缺点及使用场景

不同观点：
• **支持Excel及可视化工具的观点**：
  - Excel是成功的软件，Karen利用其技术技能和领域知识创建了对公司至关重要的系统，值得赞赏（jdauriemma）。
  - Excel是一种无需编程知识的编码工具，让非专业开发人员也能开发应用，这是积极的一面（Ezhik）。
  - 可视化工具在视觉领域（如CAD、表单设计）几乎总是胜出（mont_tag）。
  - 可视化工具让团队和个人能构建原本无法实现的东西，提供结构化解决方案并解决自动化运行中的管理问题（haswell）。

• **批评Excel及可视化工具的观点**：
  - 文章对Excel的类比不恰当，虽然Excel可能产生技术债务，但清理技术债务是值得的（jdauriemma）。
  - 可视化工具和工作流工具是绕过开发人员的变通方法，开发人员往往是成本中心而非价值中心（timr）。
  - Excel缺乏可重用性，代码难以在其他环境中复用，而一些可视化工具至少可以导出为JSON并以编程方式操作（daft_pink）。
  - 可视化工具的成功部分是因为人们变得懒惰和害怕，而非因为它们更优越（haswell）。

• **中立或综合观点**：
  - 可视化工具和Excel在个人生产力工具层面上有其价值，但更大的价值在于编排、继承、可见性、管理和安全能力（ajcp）。
  - 编程可以分为软件开发和劳动节约自动化，区分这两者是重要的（nyeah）。
  - 开发人员通常不提倡使用可视化工具，而是自己开发非可视化解决方案，但这也带来自身的问题（wiradikusuma）。

补充讨论：
- Excel和可视化工具的比较不应仅基于抽象特征，它们在实际应用中有不同的理由和价值，就像汽车和公交车虽然都能到达目的地但本质不同（haswell）。
- 可视化工具的成功原因包括：绕过中央IT或开发团队、解决自动化运行中的管理问题、以及可以通过费用卡支付而不需要额外预算（haswell）。
- 最终，虽然专业开发人员构建的“正确”解决方案可能更优越，但如果只有通过Excel或可视化工具管道才能实现某些功能，那么这些工具的价值就不可忽视（haswell）。

争议焦点：
- Excel和可视化工具是否仅仅是绕过开发人员的低效解决方案，还是它们在某些场景下具有独特的价值。
- 清理Excel产生的技术债务是否值得，还是应该从一开始就避免使用Excel。

Every Visual Workflow Tool is Just Excel for Developers Who Gave Up
Mohamed Ali Ben Othmen
5 min read
·
3 hours ago
--
Listen
Share
There’s a saying that goes “when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail.” But what happens when you trade your hammer for a Fisher-Price toy hammer and convince yourself it’s an upgrade? That’s exactly what’s happening with visual workflow tools, and I’m tired of pretending it’s not insane.
Every visual workflow tool like Zapier, Microsoft Power Automate, make.com, whatever flavor-of-the-month platform you’re using is just Excel for developers who’ve given up on being developers. And just like Excel, they’re creating a special kind of hell that someone else (probably you, six months from now) will have to deal with.
The Excel Comparison Isn’t an Insult, It’s a Warning
Think about it. Excel and visual workflow tools are fundamentally the same: point-and-click interfaces that let people build complex logic without understanding what they’re actually building. Excel uses cells and formulas, visual workflows use boxes and connectors, but the principle is identical. Both promise to make hard things easy. Both create dependency webs that become absolute nightmares to debug. Both give dangerous amounts of power to people who have no idea what they’re unleashing.
You know what happens with Excel. Karen from accounting builds a “simple” spreadsheet to track expenses. Six months later, it’s a 47-sheet monster with circular references and VLOOKUP formulas that would make a mathematician weep. The company depends on it, nobody understands it, and when it breaks (not if, when), guess who gets called to fix it?
Visual workflows are the same story, just with more colorful boxes and higher monthly fees.
The Question That Should Keep You Up at Night
Here’s what I don’t understand: why are developers whose literal job is to write, understand, and debug code are willingly trading their superpower for drag-and-drop boxes?
Code is infinitely more powerful. You can version control it, test it, refactor it, and when something breaks, you get actual error messages instead of “Node 47 failed.” You can build exactly what you need, scale it however you want, and integrate it with literally anything that has an API.
So why are we choosing tools that are objectively worse at being code? Why are we paying money to make ourselves less capable?
The Uncomfortable Truths We Don’t Want to Admit
Let’s be honest about what’s really happening here. Visual workflow tools aren’t succeeding because they’re better, they’re succeeding because we’ve gotten lazy and scared.
We’ve developed imposter syndrome about our own job.
Somewhere along the way, we started thinking “maybe I’m not smart enough for ‘real’ coding.” So we reach for tools that feel easier, that don’t require us to think through proper architecture or handle edge cases.
We’re suffering from decision fatigue.
Writing code means making a thousand tiny decisions. What framework? How do I structure this? What about error handling? Visual tools reduce those choices, which feels relief until you realize you’ve also reduced your power to actually solve problems.
We’ve bought into the illusion of speed.
“Look, I can build this workflow in 5 minutes!” we say, conveniently ignoring the 5 hours we’ll spend next month trying to figure out why it randomly stopped working.
Management pressure is real.
“Can’t you just use that no-code thing so Sarah from marketing can help maintain it?” Sure, let’s give Sarah the ability to accidentally bring down our entire customer onboarding process. What could go wrong?
But the biggest truth?
We’ve gotten cognitively lazy.
Dragging boxes around feels easier than thinking through the actual problem. It’s the programming equivalent of ordering takeout every night instead of learning to cook.
The Economics Make No Sense
Here’s the part that really gets me: you’re paying premium prices for inferior tools when you literally have the skills to build better solutions for free.
You can write Python, JavaScript, or whatever language you prefer for exactly $0 and have unlimited power. Or you can pay $50+ per month to drag boxes around with artificial constraints. How does this make sense?
These platforms have you trapped in subscription models where you’re paying monthly to be locked into their limited vision of what your workflow should look like. Want to use a custom API? That’s the Enterprise plan for $500/month. Need more than 1000 operations? Upgrade time! Hit a rate limit because too many people are using their shared infrastructure? Sorry, that’s just how it works.
You’re literally paying companies to make you less capable than you naturally are. It’s like a chef paying someone to only let them use a microwave.
The Red Flags You’re Choosing to Ignore
The signs are everywhere, but we keep pretending they’re not deal-breakers:
Vendor lock-in
